title: Marquee Tool Tricks
intro: The Marquee tool selects a range of time rather than whole regions, across one track or many. Once that clicks, a lot of editing you would otherwise do by hand becomes unnecessary.

tips.d: Make Marquee your Command-click tool. In the Tracks area, click the Command-click Tool menu and choose the Marquee tool. From then on, hold ⌘ and drag to marquee-select parts of regions on one or more tracks. Release ⌘ and you're back on your Left-click tool.

tips.d: Start playback while a marquee selection is active and Logic plays from the selection's left edge to its right edge, then stops. It's the fastest way to audition a specific range without touching the locators.

tips.t: Cut a hole in every track at once
tips.d: Choose View > Marquee Ruler, then drag in the marquee ruler to select across all tracks. Delete, and only the parts of regions inside the marquee are removed, on every track, in one action.

src.label: Apple — Select parts of regions in Logic Pro for Mac

tips.t: Set the locators to the marquee instantly
tips.d: With a marquee selection active, press ⌘U (Set Locators/Loop by Regions/Events/Marquee and Enable Cycle/Loop). The cycle locators snap to the selection and Cycle turns on. Prefer the mouse? Control-click the marquee ruler and choose Set Locators by Selection and Enable Cycle.

tips.t: Marquee automation to move only that range
tips.d: With automation showing, drag a marquee across part of an automation lane, then click inside the selection. Logic creates two automation points at each edge, so you can drag that section up or down without changing anything on either side.

tips.t: Use marquee to create a drop
tips.d: Drag in the marquee ruler across the bar before a chorus to select it on every track, then delete. You get clean, arrangement-wide silence for that bar in one edit.
